judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is Select2's inner span.select2-selection__rendered (role=textbox, not focusable, read-only). It sits inside the real control, the focusable select2 combobox, and only displays the current value. The combobox points aria-labelledby and aria-controls at it. The span has title="Selecione...", which gives it a non-empty accessible name under accname step 2I. That is how axe and ACT rule e086e5 (form field has non-empty accessible name) compute the name, so the span passes. Chrome's tree in the snapshot does show name "", but the value "Selecione..." is exposed, so a screen reader would not announce only "textbox". The span is not a separate user interface component in WCAG's sense. The real 4.1.2/1.3.1 problem on this widget is that the combobox is named by its current value ("Selecione...") and not by its label "Tipo de câncer", which sits on the aria-hidden native select. The rule had the title attribute and still reported a nameless field. The live page markup is unchanged.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 13px, weight-400 paragraph "Faça você também parte desta batalha" in the light footer band (#icons-ft) under the "Doações" heading. The CSS colour is rgb(107,118,116) = #6b7674 on the band's #eef3f2. In the screenshot the darkest glyph pixel is exactly #6b7674 and the background is #eef3f2, which gives 4.19:1. That is below the 4.5:1 that 1.4.3 requires for text that is not large. The transparent overlay link (a.absolute-link) does not change the colours. On the live site the CSS still uses --color-grey #6b7674 on --color-light #eef3f2.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 13px regular footer text "Diferentes materiais educativos para download" under "Folhetos", coloured #6b7674 (CSS) on the #eef3f2 band. judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the site search box in the header. Its accessible name is aria-label "Pesquisar no Instituto Oncoguia", which plainly says what it is for. The placeholder "Pesquisar..." is pushed off screen with text-indent:-9999px. What users see is a magnifier icon and the Google "Melhorado pelo Google" branding, the usual cue for a site search. Even "Pesquisar" (Search) alone would be a descriptive label for a site search field. Nothing here fails 2.4.6. The model judged the hidden placeholder and ignored the descriptive name it was given. The live markup is unchanged.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the e-mail field of the sidebar sign-up form "Quer ficar em contato com o Oncoguia? Cadastre-se aqui", which asks for the user's own address. It has a visually hidden label "E-mail" and type=email, but autocomplete="off". The input purpose is therefore not identified as the user's email, which is one of the purposes in WCAG's Input Purposes list. type=email gives only the data format, not that the address belongs to the user, so it does not meet 1.3.5 (sufficient technique H98 needs autocomplete="email"). The live page still has autocomplete="off".

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the Select2 combobox in the sidebar card. The card title "Busque seu tipo de câncer" (Search your cancer type) sits right above it, and "Selecione..." is the default value or placeholder shown inside the box. The label users see is the card title, and it clearly describes the purpose, so 2.4.6 (labels describe purpose) is met. The real defect is programmatic. The combobox's accessible name comes from aria-labelledby on its own rendered value, so it is "Selecione..." now and becomes the chosen option later. The actual label "Tipo de câncer" is on the aria-hidden native select, and the visible title is not associated. That fails 1.3.1, 4.1.2 and arguably 2.5.3, not 2.4.6. The finding treats the accessible name as the label. The live markup is unchanged.
